drugRefs.why: First-line when bacterial criteria are met - covers S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, and beta-lactamase-producing M. catarrhalis, addressing the main bacterial causes.

drugRefs.coverage: Alternative in penicillin allergy, covering the same core pathogens.

coverageMatrix.completeness: Covers essentially all expected bacterial pathogens when treatment is indicated.
gaps: None for typical outpatient bacterial sinusitis.

stewardship.deescalation: If started empirically and the patient fails to improve in 7 days, reassess for resistant organism or alternative diagnosis rather than escalating reflexively.

drugs.why: First-line when bacterial criteria are met - covers S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, and beta-lactamase-producing M. catarrhalis, addressing the main bacterial causes.

drugs.coverage: Alternative in penicillin allergy, covering the same core pathogens.

framework: Most acute sinusitis is viral and self-limited within 7-10 days - antibiotics should be withheld until bacterial criteria are met.
Avoid routine imaging or antibiotics for uncomplicated symptoms under 10 days.
Watchful waiting for 7 days is an appropriate alternative to immediate antibiotics even when bacterial criteria are borderline, in a reliable patient who can follow up.
